notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; step 1 was correct.
Circuit follows the schematic: 5V - FSR - node (A0 or A1) - 10K - GND for each sensor; 5V - button - pin 2 - 10K - GND for the button.

Breadboard naming: the image labels the lower half rows a-e and the upper half rows f-j. The catalogue maps rows a-e to bank 't' and f-j to bank 'b', so I followed the row letters. Rails next to the a-e half (bottom of the image) are tp/tn. Rails next to the f-j half (top of the image) are bp/bn. 'p' is the + rail and 'n' is the - rail.
Rail hole numbers are approximate. Each rail is one strip, so the exact number does not change the connectivity.

Pushbutton: it straddles the centre gap at columns 5 and 7. I took side 1 as the column-5 pair (1.l upper, 1.r lower) and side 2 as the column-7 pair (2.l upper, 2.r lower). Side 1 is on 5V and side 2 is on pin 2 and the pull-down resistor.

Sensor 1: the FSR and its 10K resistor share column 6 (lower half). Wire6 (A0) is in the same column. The resistor goes to the ground rail and the FSR's other leg goes to the 5V rail. Sensor 2 is the same in column 16 with A1.
The FSR legs run directly from the breadboard to the + rail; the image shows them as red and blue leads. The two rail-link wires (black, red) join the upper and lower rails.
The Uno GND wire goes to GND.1; the image shows one of the two GND pins next to 5V.
